name: E2E Scaffolding - No Join Is Ever Published In The Clear
description:
End-to-end coverage for #3904 / #3910: an invitation join must never reach the namespace gossip topic as a cleartext `NamespaceOp::Root`.
`RootOp::MemberJoined` / `MemberJoinedAt` name an account, the group it joined and when. Topic subscription is not authorization-gated, so a cleartext join lets anyone who knows a namespace id watch a private group's membership assemble in real time. Every other root op is sealed; these two were the remaining hole, and #3910 closed it — a joiner holding the covering key seals its own join, and one that does not hands the signed op to a keyholder that publishes it as `root_relay_sealed`.
WHY THIS MARKER
The decisive signal is the `op_kind` field on governance-store's "namespace governance op published" line, because that label comes from `NamespaceOp::op_kind_label` — i.e. from the wire variant actually handed to the publisher. A sealed join publishes as `root_sealed`, `root_sealed_for_group` or `root_relay_sealed`; the labels `member_joined` / `member_joined_at` are emitted ONLY for a cleartext `NamespaceOp::Root(RootOp::MemberJoined*)`. Asserting those two are absent is therefore a direct test of the wire form, and it fails the moment anyone reintroduces a cleartext-publish fallback in `join_group`.
Deliberately NOT asserted on the log line #3910 removed. That PR deleted the `"publishing this join in the clear"` arm outright, so an `assert_log_absent` on that string would pass while testing nothing. The failure mode worth guarding is a FUTURE fallback, which would carry a new message but the same `op_kind`.
WHY THE PATTERNS MATCH THE QUOTED VALUE AND NOT `op_kind="..."`
Because a raw node log carries ANSI escapes BETWEEN a field name and its value, so `op_kind="member_joined_at"` matches nothing at all — and for an `assert_log_absent` that is not a loud failure, it is a silently vacuous pass, which is precisely the shape of gate this scenario exists to avoid becoming. The projection-coverage gate in `e2e-rust-apps.yml` hit this and now `sed`s the escapes out before grepping; merobox's log asserts grep the container output as-is, so the pattern has to stay inside one token. The Debug-rendered value `"member_joined_at"` — quotes included — is contiguous, and the quotes are what keep it from also matching `"member_joined_at_..."` or `"root_sealed"` from matching `"root_sealed_for_group"`.
The positive assertion is on the JOINER, not on node-1, and that distinction is easy to get wrong: these labels exist on the PUBLISH path only. A receiving node logs a different `op_kind` entirely — `add` / `join` / `remove`, from `MembershipOpKind::label` in `apply_signed_namespace_op.rs`. So node-1 has no `root_sealed*` line for a join it merely received, and asserting there would have matched node-1's own `GroupCreated` / `KeyDelivery` publishes instead — passing without ever testing a join.
TWO THINGS THIS DOES NOT COVER, stated rather than left to be discovered.
1. The RELAY path itself. Reaching it needs an admitter that endorses a join
   while holding no key for the covering group, and merobox has no
   declarative way to produce a keyless-but-endorsing responder — every node
   here is keyed by the time it answers. So `root_relay_sealed` is not
   asserted present. What is asserted is the property that has to hold on
   every path, relay included: no join is ever in the clear. The relay
   branch's own gate is covered by the unit tests in
   `crates/node/src/sync/manager/relay_sealed_join.rs`.
2. The SUBGROUP-targeted invitation join (`root_sealed_for_group`, #3858 /
   #3859). `POST /admin-api/namespaces/:id/invite` refuses a non-root group
   — *"namespace_id must reference a root group (namespace)"* — so a
   subgroup invitation is only reachable through the `recursive` flag, which
   the merobox `create_namespace_invitation` step does not expose. An
   admin-push `add_group_members` is not a substitute: that publishes a
   `MemberAdded` GroupOp, not a join, so it would exercise none of this.
